title: Biological Restoration
definition: The body's designed process for completing the activation cycle and settling back to baseline after a threat response.
summary: Biological Restoration is the mechanism on which the entire twelve-framework system turns. When the nervous system mobilizes for threat, the activation is designed to complete: mobilize, respond, restore. The body does not reason its way back to baseline — it restores through the same somatic channels it departed through. It cannot be forced. It can only be allowed.
aliasNote: Called 'Regulation — The Return' in the applied model (M1: The Inner Compass) on teg-blue.com. Same mechanism, applied framing.

content.title: What It Is
content.content: Biological Restoration is the body's designed completion process. When the nervous system activates for threat — heart accelerates, hormones flood, muscles brace — all of this was designed to be temporary. The body was built to complete the cycle: mobilize, respond, and restore. The activation must discharge, the breath must slow, the muscles must release, the hormones must clear. This process is closer to digestion than to exercise — it runs when it is not blocked, not when you try harder.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Maps It
content.content: Biological Restoration is the hinge of the entire twelve-framework system — step four of the seven-step arc, with three steps on each side. Everything before it is the body's designed process. Everything after depends on whether it completed. The distinction between somatic restoration (body-level activations that can complete alone) and relational restoration (belonging-based emotions that require another person staying) is a key TEG-Blue contribution. What is commonly called 'regulation' conflates two different processes: the body's designed completion and cognitive override.
